newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Murray & Roberts sinks amid profit worries.
newsitem.headline: Murray & Roberts sinks amid profit worries.

text.p: Shares in South African engineering to construction group Murray & Roberts Ltd fell on Tuesday after the firm announced that a series of one-off charges would likely see it post an attributable loss of about 275 million rand for the year to June 30.
By about 0735 GMT Murray & Roberts' stock was down 165 cents or 15 percent at 900 cents, making it the third biggest percentage loser on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
"The guys are just selling them out here following their profit warning," one dealer said.
"They had this profit warning where they say they're likely to make a loss for the year to June...and there's just a lot of selling at this stage," the dealer added.
The firm said it had reassessed the impact of future losses on existing property headleases and made a provision of 130 million rand to cover the exposure.

It said a decision had also been taken to reduce the carrying costs of various operations within Standard Engineering Ltd by 70 million rand, while a settlement with Germany's Siemens AG on a contractual dispute over the supply of wagons to Taiwan's DORTS rapid transport system had been reached.

But insurance claims relating to the dispute were unlikely to be settled soon enough for them to add value to the year results, the company said, adding its ongoing operations had performed well in the context of a tighter domestic market.
Murray & Roberts said it anticipated improvements in trading in 1998 and solid growth and continued cash generation in 1999 and 2000.
It added that it expected to maintain its total dividend for the year to June 30.
